To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the information content of an auditor switch is not fully incorporated by analysts in their forecasts; (2) the information content is greater in the case of a Big Five to national/regional switch; and (3) the information content does not vary with the size of the firm.

(1) there is a significant difference between actual earnings and the earnings forecasted by analysts when the company changes auditors from a national or regional firm to a Big Five firm and (2) there is no difference between actual earnings of the company and the earnings forecast by analysts when the Big Five firm switches to a national or regional auditor.
the market reaction to a change in auditor type is positive and significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information content associated with a change in auditor type for the client.
the information content of changes in auditor type for companies who have already chosen to have their statements audited.
the information content of the change from one type of auditor (Big Five) to another (non Big Five) and whether the market is efficient in the incorporation of this information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auditor provides assurance to third party users of the financial statements that the financial statements are in accordance with GAAP.
audited financial statements are a signal to third parties that the financial information contained in those statements are more credible.
companies hire auditors to satisfy legal requirements and to provide credibility for their financial statements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
companies that hire auditors have higher returns than companies who do not.
the auditor is an important part of the information environment of the company.
audited financial statements are perceived by investors as more credible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
companies that are audited by a Big Five firm earn a higher return than companies that are auditors by a non Big Five auditor (Beatty, 1989).
companies who hire auditors to provide an audit of their financial statements will receive a higher valuation for their company.
the market appears to react negatively to auditor changes, and this reaction is not completely explained by the change in the quality of the audit.
